Context/Background: Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (CD) is a severe gastrointestinal disorder causing extensive mucosal damage with limited treatment options. Severe manifestations of the disease appear at higher rates in non-Europeans but the genetic and cellular mechanisms driving the disease phenotypes remain poorly understood. Herein, we tested whether pathologic determinants in the epithelial stem cell compartment could be detected at the transcript level in rectal organoids derived from a diverse patient population. Rectal organoid and mucosal cells from endoscopic biopsies of each patient having perianal fistulizing CD or no disease controls were prepared for and sequenced at the single cell level. After cell type annotations based on expressed marker genes, samples were analyzed by principal components, for differential transcript expression, cell type proportions, and pathway enrichment.
Prompt: Pathway analysis of transcriptional data from the mucosal epithelial (undifferentiated) cells of different CD phenotypes was performed against the Reactome database.  CD phenotypes compared are PIF (Perianal CD inflamed) vs PNI (Perianal CD non inflamed), PIF vs Control (non IBD), and PIN vs Control.  Please give a summary of the pathway enrichment results.  Focus on comparisons involving the PIF (inflamed) group.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Single‐cell RNA‐seq was performed on mucosal epithelial (undifferentiated) cells from rectal organoids and biopsies of patients with perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (PIF), perianal non‐inflamed CD (PNI), and non‐IBD controls. Differential expression between PIF and both PNI and controls was followed by Reactome pathway enrichment (Supplemental Table 2). Details such as exact sample sizes and replicate numbers are not specified.

Keywords  
• RNA metabolism  
• Translation  
• Mitochondrial energy metabolism  
• Cellular stress responses  
• Cell cycle  

Candidate Genes  
• FAU  
• SNRPB  
• MRPL41  
• COX5A  
• CDK4  

Pathway Enrichments  
Reactome (DOWN) PIF vs Control:  
| Theme                                                        | GeneCount | Direction |  
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------|  
| METABOLISM OF RNA                                            | 105       | DOWN      |  
| TRANSLATION                                                  | 77        | DOWN      |  
| THE CITRIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND RESPIRATORY ELECTRON TRANSPORT | 74        | DOWN      |  
| CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STIMULI                                | 73        | DOWN      |  
| CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS                                 | 71        | DOWN      |  

Reactome (DOWN) PIF vs PNI:  
| Theme                                                        | GeneCount | Direction |  
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------|  
| METABOLISM OF RNA                                            | 76        | DOWN      |  
| TRANSLATION                                                  | 67        | DOWN      |  
| THE CITRIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND RESPIRATORY ELECTRON TRANSPORT | 61        | DOWN      |  
| CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STIMULI                                | 55        | DOWN      |  
| CELLULAR RESPONSES TO STRESS                                 | 53        | DOWN      |  

Analysis  
Comparison of PIF to both controls and PNI reveals a highly concordant downregulation of core “housekeeping” pathways. RNA processing (metabolism of RNA) and protein synthesis (translation) are the most suppressed, with 105 and 77 genes down in PIF vs control and 76 and 67 genes down in PIF vs PNI. Mitochondrial energy production via the TCA cycle and respiratory electron transport is similarly repressed (–74 and –61 genes), suggesting compromised bioenergetics in inflamed epithelium. Broad suppression of cellular response modules—both general stimuli and chemical/stress responses—indicates an impaired ability to handle physiological stress. Downregulation of these processes likely underlies reduced proliferative and reparative capacity in the PIF epithelial stem cell compartment.  

Targeted (keyword‐guided) subset  
Filtering for our keywords (RNA, translation, mitochondrial, stress, cell cycle) did not yield unique pathways beyond those already highlighted, confirming that PIF‐linked enrichment is dominated by downregulation of RNA metabolism, translation, mitochondrial energy metabolism, stress responses, and cell cycle processes.  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Upregulated: not observed (no UP entries reported)  
Downregulated:  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                     | Pathway(s)                              |  
|--------|-----------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|  
| FAU    | DOWN      | Ubiquitin‐like modifier (ubiquitylation) | Metabolism of RNA; Stress responses      |  
| SNRPB  | DOWN      | Core spliceosomal factor          | Metabolism of RNA; mRNA splicing        |  
| MRPL41 | DOWN      | Mitochondrial ribosomal protein   | Translation; Mitochondrial translation  |  
| COX5A  | DOWN      | Cytochrome c oxidase subunit      | TCA cycle & respiratory electron transport |  
| CDK4   | DOWN      | Cell cycle kinase                 | Cellular responses; Cell cycle          |  

Implications  
Inflamed perianal CD epithelial cells exhibit coordinated downregulation of transcriptional, translational, metabolic, and cell‐cycle machinery—signatures of impaired regeneration and bioenergetic failure. Therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring mitochondrial function or enhancing stress‐response pathways may bolster epithelial resilience in PIF.  

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Verify whether upregulated pathways emerge at relaxed FDR thresholds or in specific epithelial subtypes.  
2. Assess functional rescue of mitochondrial respiration in PIF organoids (e.g., by PGC‐1α agonists).  
3. Measure cell‐cycle kinetics and proliferation markers in PIF vs PNI epithelial cells.  
4. Determine if similar pathway suppression occurs in differentiated epithelial subsets.
